meta.title: Energy index calculator — check your transport surcharge
meta.description: Free, no sign-up: enter your contract formula, your indices and the invoiced rate, and get the gap. Diesel, gas or electricity.

fuel.h1: Is your energy surcharge calculated correctly?
fuel.lede: Enter your contract formula, the indices for the period and the rate applied on your invoice. You get the gap straight away, in points and in euros. The same calculation covers contracts indexed on gas or electricity.
fuel.privacy: The calculation runs entirely in your browser. No data is sent, stored or kept. No sign-up is required.

energy.label: Indexed energy
energy.help: The formula is the same whatever the energy: only the reference index changes.

baseAmount.label: Base amount excluding VAT for the period
baseAmount.help: The transport amount before the energy surcharge, for one shipment or for the whole month.

energyShare.label: Energy share set in the contract
energyShare.help: The share of the price treated as sensitive to energy costs.

hints.diesel: For diesel, most often between 20 and 35%.
hints.gas: Use the share written into your contract: no settled market practice exists yet for CNG and LNG.
hints.electric: Use the share written into your contract: no settled market practice exists yet for electric.

baseIndex.label: Base index (contractual reference)
baseIndex.help: The index the contract sets as the starting point for indexation.

periodIndex.label: Index for the invoiced period
periodIndex.help: The index published for the month the invoice covers.

invoicedRate.label: Surcharge rate applied on the invoice
invoicedRate.help: The surcharge percentage the carrier charged you.

indexHints.diesel: For professional diesel, the indices published by the Comité National Routier are the ones most commonly used in France. Others exist: use the one your contract names.
indexHints.gas: Contracts indexed on CNG or LNG refer to specific indices, sometimes proprietary to the supplier. Use the one your contract names.
indexHints.electric: Contracts indexed on electricity refer to a market index or a supplier tariff. Use the one your contract names.

errors.required: This field is needed for the calculation.
errors.positive: Enter a number greater than zero.

result.title: Result

verdict.aligned: The invoiced rate matches your formula. No significant gap for this period.
verdict.overcharged: The invoiced rate is above the expected rate. For this period the difference is {amount}.
verdict.undercharged: The invoiced rate is below the expected rate. For this period the difference is {amount} in your favour.

result.annualHint: Carried across twelve months of similar volumes, this gap would represent roughly {amount}.

formula.title: How the calculation works
formula.expression: Surcharge rate = energy share × (period index − base index) ÷ base index
formula.explanation: This is the most widespread indexation formula in road transport contracts, whatever the energy. It applies the relative movement of the index to the fraction of the price treated as sensitive to energy costs.
formula.caveat: If your contract uses a different mechanism — a rolling average over several months, a trigger threshold, quarterly revision, indexation on an observed price rather than an index — the result above is only an approximation. Check the clause before raising it with your carrier.

source.title: Which index should you use?
source.body:
The one your contract names, and only that one: changing the index changes the result. Indices are many, and depend on the energy as much as on the contract.
For professional diesel, the indices published by the Comité National Routier are the ones most commonly used in France. Others exist, published by trade federations, by energy suppliers or by INSEE, and some contracts use a jointly observed price rather than an index.
source.note: CarrierBridge redistributes no index. You enter the value you have looked up, and it never leaves your browser.

fuel.disclaimer: This tool gives an indication of the calculation. It is neither legal advice nor a contractual analysis, and it does not certify that an invoice is correct. A gap found is a point to raise with your carrier.

cta.h2: Twelve months of invoices, every carrier, in one go
cta.text: This calculator handles one line at a time. In CarrierBridge you enter your formula once — for each energy and each contract — and the gap is tracked automatically, month after month, carrier by carrier, alongside your rate sheets and ancillary charges.
